newsitem.title: GERMANY: TENNIS-BECKER BACK ON WINING TRAIL.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-BECKER BACK ON WINING TRAIL.

text.p: Boris Becker won his first ATP match for almost three months on Wednesday when he beat 19-year-old fellow German Nicolas Kiefer 7-5 6-2 in the second round of the clay-court German Open.

Former world number one Becker has been suffering with a long-term wrist injury but came through without incident against a player he has been coaching recently in his role as head of the national training squad.
"It could have been a difficult match for both players but I think we did it right and avoided any funny moments," Becker said.

He had a scare while serving for the match as he fell and landed with much of his weight on his troublesome wrist but suffered no damage. "I'm okay but I didn't feel good for a few moments," the German said.
Becker, who surprisingly lost to Italian Renzo Furlan in the first round at Monte Carlo two weeks ago, produced a reasonably consistent performance.
He had some alarms in the sixth game of the opening set when he dropped serve but he broke back immediately.
He broke again at 5-5 after Kiefer had tried an ambitious serve and volley at 30-40 and found himself stranded by Becker's pass.
After Becker had served out to love for the first set he looked much more in control, breaking Kiefer three times with just one break back.
"Obviously this surface, clay, is the hardest on which to come back but I have to come back some time," Becker said.

"I will feel better and fitter if I can win a couple of matches. When you have such a serious injury and in such an important spot for a tennis player there are always days when you still feel it, especially when it is cold. But once I am healthy I am convinced it is just a question of time before I play good tennis again, though just how good I don't know."
